help.part.you.title: Your own account
help.part.you.blurb: The things that are yours rather than the family's.
help.my-profile.title: My Profile
help.my-profile.summary: Your name, how relatives reach you, and the settings for your sign-in.
help.my-profile.sections.heading: The five sections
help.my-profile.sections.b0: The rail across the top of the page switches between them. Each saves on its own, so you can fill in one and come back later.
help.my-profile.sections.b1.i0.text: Name, preferred name, phone, email, birthday, and your photo.
help.my-profile.sections.b1.i1.text: Where you live. Used by the Directory and by anything the family posts to you.
help.my-profile.sections.b1.i2.text: T-shirt size, chapter, and the other details events and reports ask for.
help.my-profile.sections.b1.i3.text: What your family may contact you about and how — a switch per notification, per channel.
help.my-profile.sections.b1.i4.text: The address you sign in with, and your password.
help.my-profile.notifications.heading: Notifications
help.my-profile.notifications.b0: **Notifications** is a grid: a row for each thing your family can contact you about, and a column for each way it could reach you — **Email**, **SMS** and **Push Notification**. Each cell is one press, **On** or **Off**, and it saves the moment you press it. There is nothing to submit.
help.my-profile.notifications.b1: It uses the email address and mobile number already in your **General** details. Both are shown at the top of the screen so you can see where a notification would go, and changing either one there changes it for every notification at once. This screen never asks you for a second number.
help.my-profile.notifications.b2.i0.text: Your family raises a check-in during a storm, an evacuation or an emergency and asks whether you are safe. Email is on unless you turn it off; SMS is off unless you turn it on.
help.my-profile.notifications.b3: **Email is on by default and SMS is not**, and that is deliberate rather than inconsistent. A check-in that reaches nobody is the thing worth avoiding, and your family already has your address — but a text has to be agreed to before anybody sends one, so nothing about SMS is ever on because you did not notice it.
help.my-profile.notifications.b4: **Push Notification** says **Not built yet** on every row. The column is there so you can see what is coming rather than being surprised by it later; nothing in the product sends one today.
help.my-profile.notifications-delivery.h: When On does not mean it will arrive
help.my-profile.notifications-delivery.b: A switch says what you have asked for. Whether we can actually deliver it is a separate question, and the screen says so underneath the grid rather than letting **On** imply more than it should.
No email address on file, or only a placeholder one — nothing marked on for Email can arrive. Add a real address under **General**.
No mobile number on file — nothing marked on for SMS can arrive.
A mobile number we have not confirmed yet — we send a six-digit code to it before we text you anything.
Text messages not switched on yet at our end. You can record your choice now and we will start using it as soon as they are.
help.my-profile.notifications-stopping.b: Turning the **SMS** cell off stops them immediately, with nothing to confirm and no reason asked for. You can turn it back on whenever you like.

Replying **STOP** to any text we send stops them too — and that one is different in a way worth knowing about. It is your mobile network that acts on it, not us, so we cannot switch it back on from this page and neither can anybody in your family. The cell says **Stopped** rather than offering a switch. If you want them back, text **START** to the number that messaged you.
help.my-profile.per-family.heading: One profile per family
help.my-profile.per-family.b0: If you belong to more than one family, you have a separate profile in each. Editing this page changes the family you are currently viewing and nothing else — which is deliberate, because the address you give your in-laws is not always the one you give your cousins.
help.my-profile.chapter.heading: Your chapter
help.my-profile.chapter.b0: The block headed with your family's name holds one field that belongs to that family alone: which **Chapter** you are in. It appears only once the family has created some; if it has not, the block says so.
help.my-profile.chapter.b1: It decides two things. Any sons or daughters under 18 who have no account of their own move with you — everybody else in the family is their own person and keeps the chapter they are in — and it can decide what you owe, because a family can attach dues to one region or one chapter. Choosing nothing leaves you under **National**: you owe the family-wide dues and none of the local ones. See [regions and chapters](/help/regions-and-chapters#dues).
help.my-profile.chapter.b2: A child whose date of birth has not been recorded does not move, because nothing on file says they are under 18. Add it on their record, or set their chapter for them from Members & Access.
help.my-profile.password.heading: Changing your password
help.my-profile.password.b0.i1: Type your current password, then the new one twice.
help.my-profile.password.b0.i2: If a code is emailed to you, type it in.
help.my-profile.password.b0.i3: Save. Every other device signed in as you is signed out.
help.my-profile.password.b1: There is also a **Sign out other devices** control on its own, for when you have simply left yourself signed in somewhere and do not want to change anything else.
help.my-profile.photo.heading: Your photo
help.my-profile.photo.b0: The photo you upload on **General** is what appears beside your name in the top bar, on the dashboard greeting, and anywhere the family sees you. Without one you get your initials.
help.my-profile.photo.b1.i1: Press the camera on the circle at the top of the page.
help.my-profile.photo.b2: A JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 2 MB. Anything else is refused with a line saying why rather than failing silently, and a new photo replaces the one it follows.
help.my-profile.photo.b3: Your photo is ONE photo, shared by every family you belong to — unlike the rest of this page, which is per family. Anybody who can see you in the [Directory](/community/directory) can see it, so it is the one field here to treat as public within the family.
help.my-profile.photo.b4: Whether it is SHOWN depends on the family’s plan, and that is decided per family rather than per account: a family whose plan does not include profile pictures shows your initials everywhere instead, and offers no camera on this page. If you belong to two families you may well see your photo in one and your initials in the other. Nothing is lost either way — the picture is still there, and it appears the moment a family’s plan includes it.
help.my-families.title: My Families
help.my-families.summary: Every family your account belongs to, which one opens by default, and how to add another.
help.my-families.reading.heading: Reading the list
help.my-families.reading.b0: Each family shows its name, its code, and where you stand in it. Two markers matter:
help.my-families.reading.b1.i0.text: The family the rest of the product is currently showing you.
help.my-families.reading.b1.i1.text: The family that opens when you sign in. Press **Default** on any other row to move it.
help.my-families.switching.heading: Switching family
help.my-families.switching.b0: Use the family switcher in the top bar — it does the same job from every page. Switching rebuilds the whole page for the new family: anything half-typed is discarded rather than carried across, which is what stops a form filled in for one family being saved into another.
help.my-families.adding.heading: Adding another family
help.my-families.adding.b0: **Join a family** takes a family code and puts you in that family's queue. **Create a family** starts a new one with you as its first member. Neither disturbs the families you are already in.
